newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov sees consensus on revenues by March 10.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov sees consensus on revenues by March 10.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki, who has forecast that next year's revenues will only be about one-third of the bonanza the Assembly expects, said Tuesday he expected to soon reach a revenue forecast consensus with lawmakers.

The Republican governor, whose Administration last year set a national record when it failed to approve a budget until 104 days after it was due, also appeared upbeat about the prospects that the state would not make such a poor showing with the fiscal 1998 budget, due April 1.
Asked if it were possible that a budget would be reached on time, Pataki told reporters in Albany, "We have an understanding that it's possible. We should have an agreement on revenues by March 10."

Pataki has estimated that the state will get an extra $650 million from late February until the end of the 1998 fiscal year, largely because Wall Street banks and brokerage houses are expected to keep earning big profits.

The Democrat-controlled Assembly, whose recent revenue forecasts have been more accurate than the governor's, looks for a $2 billion windfall, though it bases its projection on an assumption that Wall Street's financial sector would stay strong even if the stock market turned down. Financial analysts have questioned that premise, however.

The estimates produced by the Senate, which is led by Republicans, are much more conservative than the Assembly's, as the upper house looks for revenues to surge $922 million over the initial estimates.
